expectations.text: The response distinguishes supplied facts, likely causes, and unverified repository/runtime evidence, and does not claim that tests or profiling were run.
expectations.evidence: The artifact responsibly calls the duplicate behavior "consistent with" static delegate retention and explicitly says tests/profiling were not run, but it never separates the supplied scenario facts from repository/runtime facts that remain uninspected. Because this is a compound requirement, the missing evidence classification fails it.

expectations.text: The selected solution is one bounded feature-level design with explicit publisher, state, HUD, audio, save-statistics, and scene/session ownership; it does not require a global bus, Service Locator, or third-party container.
expectations.evidence: It selects an instance-scoped Health.Changed event plus three adapters. Its ownership table covers Health/player, HUD/gameplay UI, audio/player or scene, statistics/session or scene, and gameplay composition, while explicitly rejecting a global bus, Singleton/Service Locator, and DI framework.

expectations.text: The response connects duplicate delivery to static-event and Domain-Reload-disabled lifetime risk, and defines symmetric subscribe/unsubscribe plus an explicit static reset or removal of static ownership.
expectations.evidence: It connects retained static delegates and disabled Domain Reload to accumulated listeners, requires named symmetric OnEnable/OnDisable or Bind/Unbind behavior, removes the old static delegate, and gives any unrelated unavoidable static event an explicit SubsystemRegistration reset.

expectations.text: The implementation boundary keeps health rules/state testable independently from Unity-facing HUD, audio, save, and lifecycle adapters without forcing an interface or pattern for every class.
expectations.evidence: Health exposes only state and a value notification, while HUD, audio, statistics, persistence, networking, and lifecycle wiring are separate adapters. The response asks for existing interfaces/components and a small presenter rather than a framework or interface for every class.

expectations.text: The test plan starts from a failing behavioral seam and covers repeated gameplay-menu-gameplay cycles, disable/enable or destroy cleanup, duplicate delivery, and the project's Domain Reload configuration across appropriate plain C#/EditMode/PlayMode tests.
expectations.evidence: It starts with a regression reproducing enable/load/disable/reload, then lists state and adapter EditMode checks plus PlayMode enable-disable-enable, gameplay-menu-gameplay, despawn/respawn, and networking cases. It separately requires a manual repeated-Play-Mode check with Domain Reload disabled and explains the limit of an ordinary PlayMode test.

expectations.text: At least two credible alternatives are rejected with concrete trade-offs, and the response states a measurable or structural condition that would justify revisiting the choice.
expectations.evidence: Six alternatives are rejected with concrete lifetime, scope, or cost trade-offs. Revisit criteria include cross-scene consumers, replay/rollback requirements, repeated dynamic-binding duplication, prediction/reconciliation needs, and measured target-hardware cost.

expectations.text: Performance is treated honestly: no improvement is asserted without a baseline, and any optimization claim is deferred to a representative build or target-device measurement plan.
expectations.evidence: It says no profiler capture is needed for the correctness refactor, makes no speedup claim, and defers performance conclusions to target-hardware profiling if the signal becomes high volume or listener work becomes expensive.

claims.claim: The recommended change removes the static health signal in favor of an instance event and three adapters.
claims.evidence: The opening recommendation, ownership table, implementation boundaries, and rejected alternatives all maintain this same design.

claims.claim: Static delegate retention is the demonstrated root cause of the observed duplicate callbacks.
claims.evidence: The artifact only says the symptom is consistent with this cause; no source inspection, runtime capture, or transcript is available.

claims.claim: The proposed tests and profiling were not represented as completed.
claims.evidence: The testing section explicitly calls them proposed checks and states that no tests or profiling were run. No execution transcript was available for independent process verification.

eval_feedback.overall: The assertions are substantive. The baseline's single failure reflects missing evidence classification, not a weak presence-only check.
